title: KMS/HSM Secrets Shim Terraform module with automated rotation + healthchecks for VPC deployments
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background:
We need a reusable Terraform module that provisions a lightweight 'secrets shim' in customer VPCs/private deployments to enable KMS/HSM-backed secrets management across multiple backends (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault). This shim will provide envelope-wrapping using customer-managed KMS keys backed by HSM (CloudHSM or third-party HSMs), automated rotation orchestration, and an observable healthcheck endpoint so Redwood Console & ops can verify key+secret availability for Private deployments.

Problem statement:
- Current customers running Private deployments require a repeatable IaC pattern to wire KMS/HSM keys into secrets backends and application IAM roles without ad-hoc scripts.
- Rotation and reconciliation between Vault and cloud secrets stores is manual or split across multiple modules.
- We lack a standard healthcheck that surfaces HSM connectivity and key access from the VPC to Redwood monitoring.

Proposal (high level):
Create terraform-modules/kms-hsm-secrets-shim which provisions:
1) KMS key resources and HSM attachments where applicable (eg. CloudHSM cluster resources, key import or external key references).
2) An optional Vault-side configuration: transit key or KV mount + auth method bindings (IAM auth/aws auth or Kubernetes auth for in-cluster deployments).
3) Integrations with cloud secrets stores (AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager) to create wrapped secrets referencing the KMS key when requested.
4) A small shim service (container) as an optional module output that runs in the customer's VPC (ECS/Fargate or kube), exposing a /healthz and /status endpoint which verifies: key policy retrieval, HSM connectivity, ability to decrypt/unwrap a sample envelope, and Vault auth token refresh.
5) Rotation orchestration primitives (Terraform-managed schedules + guides for enabling AWS native rotation or Vault rotation jobs). The module will include TF variables to choose the rotation mechanism.
6) Outputs and IAM roles/policies that can be consumed by other modules (eg. private-deploy-apps) so apps can request unwrapped secrets via the shim or directly via Vault with correct permissions.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Vault Transit vs direct KV: Transit keeps plaintext out of Vault and suits envelope patterns, but requires an extra layer for apps that expect secret values. We will default to Transit for HSM-backed KMS envelope support and provide a flag to enable KV for migrations.
- Managed KMS vs imported HSM keys: For on-prem HSM customers we will support ExternalKey material references and a key reference path rather than creating keys. For cloud HSM we will provision CloudHSM clusters only when "manage_hsm"=true.
- Shim service: Running a small container increases maintenance surface but provides a consistent healthcheck and local caching for low-latency reads; the service will be optional and we will publish a minimal binary for air-gapped installs.

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied before merging):
- Module can provision keys (or bind to external keys) and produce IAM roles/policies which grant decrypt/encrypt to a provided role.
- Module can create a Vault transit key and bind the Vault policy so the shim can use it.
- Shim container image and Helm/ECS task definition are included and can be deployed in a test VPC with Terraform only.
- Health endpoint returns 200 with a detailed health blob (key policy ok, HSM connected, transit active) within 5s after deploy in a non-degraded environment.
- Rotation can be triggered via TF toggle and performs a safe key rotation workflow with no loss of availability in a canary test.
- CI tests validate module outputs, run a terraform apply/destroy against a mocked or short-lived test account, and exercise the /healthz endpoint.

Planned tasks (implementation plan):
- 1) Design doc + security review (Confluence) — list required policies and HSM onboarding steps.
- 2) Module skeleton (variables/outputs) and IAM policy templates.
- 3) Vault integration: example policy, transit key creation, and vault role.
- 4) Shim implementation: small Go service + container, health endpoints, TLS, minimal metrics (Prometheus).
- 5) Terraform resources for CloudHSM conditional provisioning and external key references.
- 6) CI + integration test harness (short-lived accounts or local emulation using moto/vault dev cluster).
- 7) Docs and example consumption pattern for private-deploy apps.
- 8) Security review and rollout plan for existing Private customers (migration playbook).

Design & artifact links:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/KMS-HSM+Secrets+Shim
- Terraform module repo (initial PR): https://github.com/redwood/terraform-modules/pull/4123
- Shim service repo (proto): https://github.com/redwood/secrets-shim
- Example usage: https://terraform.redwood.ai/modules/kms-hsm-secrets-shim

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for shim logic (key wrap/unwrap paths), e2e integration tests deploying to a CI test account with a short-lived CloudHSM cluster where permitted.
- Smoke test will call /healthz immediately after deploy and assert all checks pass.
- Nightly CI will run a rotation scenario to validate seamless rewrap and consumer read capability.

Rollout & upgrade notes:
- Module will be versioned semantically. Major changes (key algorithm, default rotation semantics) will be major bumps.
- Backwards compatibility: module defaults to creating new KMS keys only when "create_kms_key"=true; if false it will accept a key_id. Migration guide will include an automated sweep to backfill role policies and expected downtime windows for customer-managed keys.

Open questions / blockers:
- Determine the standard approach for supporting hardware-backed keys for on-prem HSM vendors (YubiHSM vs Thales). Action: Security to confirm supported HSM vendors (owner: Priya Singh, due 2026-02-27).
- CI permissions to spin up CloudHSM in the Redwood test org; blocked on cloud infra team (ENG-20987).

Estimated risk & mitigation:
- Risk: HSM onboarding complexity across customers. Mitigation: provide a small operator-run checklist and fallback to KMS envelope only for customers who cannot provide HSM.
- Risk: secret exposure during rotation. Mitigation: integration tests and canary rotation policy, ensure all operations are recorded in audit logs.

Notes and links to follow-ups:
- See RFC for healthcheck schema: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Healthcheck+Schemas
- Follow-up task to add Console dashboard panel for shim instances (ENG-21772).
